critical.q: Which of the following describes the yeast profile of a classic German Weissbier (10A)?
critical.exp: Weissbier yeast provides signature banana (isoamyl acetate) and clove (4-vinylguaiacol).

critical.q: What distinguishes an American Porter (20A) from an Irish Stout (15B)?
options: American Porter lacks the sharp roasted barley acrid bite
American Porter uses exclusively European malts
critical.exp: Irish Stouts are defined by roasted unmalted barley astringency; American Porters rely on chocolate/caramel malts and clean hop bitterness.

critical.q: What is the defining malt character of a Doppelbock (9A)?
options: Intense, rich Maillard products, toasty, dark fruit
critical.exp: Doppelbocks rely on rich Munich and Vienna malts undergoing extensive Maillard reactions during mashing/boiling.

critical.q: Which hop variety is most authentic for a Czech Premium Pale Lager (3B)?
critical.exp: Saaz hops provide the classic spicy, floral, and herbal aroma of Czech pale lagers.

options: Pale, highly attenuated (dry), spicy/fruity, high ABV
critical.exp: Tripels are pale and dry, utilizing highly attenuative yeast and clear candi sugar.

critical.q: What is the primary difference between German Pils (5D) and Czech Premium Pale Lager (3B)?
options: German Pils is darker and sweeter
German Pils is drier, crisper, lighter in body, and higher in carbonation
Czech Pils uses exclusively ale yeast
critical.exp: German Pils is drier, crisper, and more bitter due to sulfate water profiles and higher attenuation.

critical.q: Which malt profile is essential for an authentic Märzen (6A)?
options: Rich toasted German Munich and Vienna malts without roast or caramel
critical.exp: Märzen relies on German Munich and Vienna malts for elegant, bready, toasted flavor.

critical.q: What defines the bitterness profile of a Double IPA (22A)?
options: Assertive and high (60-120 IBU) supported by clean pale malts and high attenuation
critical.exp: Double IPAs showcase massive, clean hop bitterness drying out via sugar additions.

critical.q: What is the acceptable diacetyl level in a Czech Premium Pale Lager (3B)?
options: Low to trace levels are acceptable and traditional
critical.exp: Low to trace diacetyl is permissible in Czech lagers, adding rounded mouthfeel.

critical.q: Which parameters distinguish Best Bitter (11B) from Strong Bitter (11C)?
options: Best Bitter is stronger in alcohol
Best Bitter has lower gravity (1.040-1.048) and alcohol (3.8-4.6%) than Strong Bitter
Strong Bitter is a dark stout
critical.exp: Best Bitter is a session pub ale, whereas Strong Bitter (ESB) scales up in gravity, alcohol, and hop bite.

tf.q: True or False: A judge may assign a score of 12 to a beer that is completely infected and undrinkable.
tf.exp: False. The lowest permissible floor score for a beer evaluated in a BJCP competition is 13.

tf.q: True or False: To achieve the rank of Master, a judge must score at least a 90 on both the Tasting Exam and the Written Exam.
tf.exp: True. Master status requires a minimum 90% score on both exams in addition to experience points.

tf.q: True or False: If a beer is entered into the wrong subcategory, the judge should evaluate it as the style it most resembles.
tf.exp: False. Beers must be judged strictly against the specific subcategory in which they were entered.

tf.q: True or False: A minimum of 20 experience points (including 10 judging points) is required to sit for the National Exam.
tf.exp: True. National level prerequisites require 20 total points.

tf.q: True or False: Non-BJCP judges may judge in a sanctioned competition if paired with an experienced BJCP judge.
tf.exp: True. Novice or non-BJCP judges are routinely paired with experienced judges for training.

tf.q: True or False: A score of 38-44 on a scoresheet designates an 'Excellent' example of the style.
tf.exp: True. The score ranges are: Outstanding (45-50), Excellent (38-44), Very Good (30-37), Good (21-29), Fair (14-20), Problematic (13).

tf.q: True or False: Black or dark blue ink is required on BJCP scoresheets.
tf.exp: True. Red or light-colored pens are prohibited as they do not scan or copy clearly.

tf.q: True or False: Diacetyl rest involves raising lager fermentation temperatures near the end of primary fermentation.
tf.exp: True. Raising the temperature to 62-65°F (17-18°C) encourages yeast to reabsorb diacetyl.

tf.q: True or False: If two judges disagree by more than 7 points, they must discuss and reconcile their scores.
tf.exp: True. The standard 7-point consensus rule requires judges to discuss and adjust scores.

tf.q: True or False: Skunky odor in beer is caused by autolysis of dead yeast cells.
tf.exp: False. Skunkiness (lightstruck) is caused by UV light breaking down hop alpha acids into 3-methyl-2-butene-1-thiol.

mead.q: Which honey variety is uniquely noted for having a natural 'waxy' character?
mead.exp: Alfalfa honey naturally presents a beeswax and hay aroma.

mead.q: What physical characteristic is unique to Tupelo honey?
options: High ratio of fructose to glucose preventing crystallization
mead.exp: Tupelo honey rarely crystallizes due to its naturally high fructose ratio.

options: A mead made with caramelized or burned honey
mead.exp: Bochet involves boiling/caramelizing honey prior to fermentation to create marshmallow, toffee, and burnt sugar flavors.

options: A mead fermented with malted grain and honey
mead.exp: Braggot is a historical style blending malted barley and honey.

mead.q: Why are staggered nutrient additions (TOSNA/YAN) crucial in high-gravity mead fermentations?
options: To prevent fusel alcohol production and stuck fermentations
mead.exp: Honey lacks free amino nitrogen (FAN), requiring phased additions of organic nutrients to prevent yeast stress.

options: A French method to create naturally sweet cider by starving yeast of nutrients
Freezing apple juice to concentrate sugar
Adding sulfur dioxide to kill wild bacteria
cider.exp: Keeving forms a pectin gel 'chapeau brun' that strips nitrogen/nutrients, halting fermentation naturally to leave residual sugar.

cider.q: What sugar alcohol naturally present in perry pears imparts a sweet perception even in bone-dry perry?
cider.exp: Sorbitol is unfermentable by wine/cider yeast, providing residual sweetness and slick mouthfeel in perry.

cider.q: What is an 'escanciar' pour in Spanish cider service?
options: Pouring Spanish cider from height to aerate and release CO2/volatiles
Barrel aging cider in sherry casks
Blending sweet and sharp apple juice
cider.exp: Escanciar is the traditional Asturian method of pouring cider overhead into a glass held low.

options: Cider made from freeze-concentrated apple juice with no added sugar
Cider fermented with lager yeast at freezing temperatures
cider.exp: Ice ciders concentrate natural apple sugars via ambient freeze distillation of juice or apples before fermentation.

cider.q: Which apple category provides high tannin and low acidity?
cider.exp: Bittersweet apples provide high tannin/astringency and low malic acid.
